title: Collider Detector Observables from Lattice Spin Systems
authors: João Barata, Ying-Ying Li, Bo Wang, Hua Xing Zhu
abstract: Detector observables pose a fundamental challenge for nonperturbative lattice methods due to their intrinsically real-time and asymptotic nature. We propose quantum simulation platforms as an ideal setting for studying these observables. Using quantum spin systems as a demonstration, we construct lattice detector operators and establish their connection to continuum energy-flow observables. We demonstrate this framework in the $1+1$-dimensional quantum Ising model, where finite lattice calculations show quantitative agreement with conformal field theory expectations at criticality. These results support the interpretation of the lattice flow operators as regulated counterparts of continuum detectors in the scaling and asymptotic limits, providing a concrete route toward realizing high-energy collider physics on table-top quantum platforms.
summary: This work proposes using quantum spin systems to simulate complex detector observables from high-energy physics. By mapping lattice operators to continuum CFT predictions, the authors demonstrate that advanced numerical techniques successfully reproduce theoretical expectations at critical points. This provides a concrete roadmap for realizing collider physics simulations on tabletop quantum hardware.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fundamental challenge of calculating detector observables in Quantum Field Theory (QFT) because these observables are intrinsically real-time and asymptotic.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that lattice constructions for energy-flow observables in the 1+1D Ising model show quantitative agreement with Conformal Field Theory (CFT) predictions at criticality.
method: They construct lattice detector operators and use advanced numerical techniques like DMRG and TEBD to simulate real-time evolution and calculate correlators, comparing results against CFT predictions.
model_or_system: The study uses quantum spin systems, specifically the 1+1-dimensional transverse-field Ising model, as a platform to simulate high-energy physics phenomena.
key_observables: Detector observables, energy-flow operators $E(\hat{n})$, multi-point correlators $\langle E(\hat{n}_1) \cdots E(\hat{n}_k) angle$, and one-point energy fractions ($F_R$).
important_parameters: The critical point ($g=1$), the lattice spacing ($a_l$), the source-detector separation ($R_{	ext{det}}$), and time evolution parameters ($\delta t$).
main_assumptions: The method relies on the controlled setting provided by the critical point for quantitative benchmarking, and some calculations assume boundary effects are negligible.
figures_summary: Figures compare CFT predictions (solid markers) against DMRG/simulation extractions (translucent markers) for operator decompositions and two-point functions, showing agreement at criticality.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical connection between lattice operators and continuum CFT observables, details the numerical implementation using DMRG/TEBD for both static and real-time calculations, and validates the framework by comparing results across different coupling regimes.
why_interesting: The direct application of numerical methods (DMRG, TEBD) to model high-energy physics observables like energy flow provides a concrete, testable pathway for quantum simulation platforms.
